title: Incident opening — written update
situation: In a technical discussion, the team has just observed an error spike. You must write the decision accurately without overstating the evidence.
instructions: Write four sentences opening an incident with the observation, the current impact, the unknown, and the next update time.

vocabulary.meaning: a statement of what is currently observed and what is not yet known, published before the cause is understood
the commitment that ends an incident message, which prevents the audience from asking and lets the responders work

expectedElements: The observation is separated from the interpretation
The current impact is stated in user terms
A next update time is committed to
modelAnswer: Since 14:10 the checkout error rate has risen from under one percent to approximately twelve percent. Users see a failure when confirming an order, while existing orders are unaffected. The cause is not yet known and I am deliberately not naming one until the evidence separates our two candidate explanations, which would lead to different actions. Three engineers are investigating and the next update will be sent at 14:40 regardless of progress.
commonMistakes: Naming a cause in the opening message before it is established
Ending the message without committing to a next update time
variants: Rewrite the update for customers rather than for the internal channel.
